title: POC weekly - caching sync

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 15:00 PDT | Duration 42m | Attendees: Lina Park, Omar Reyes, Carlos Nguyen (Redwood) / Sofia Martinez, Raj Patel, Maya Chen (BrightCart)

Summary/Notes: quick recap at top, auto generated may be imperfect

00:00 Lina: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly caching sync for the BrightCart POC, Lina from Redwood, Omar's here, Carlos is on for notes. Sofia, Raj, Maya, you there?
00:08 Sofia: yep thanks, hi all, we got a couple items today, mostly around the hit rates and the prompt reuse work we started last week.
00:14 Omar: cool, I'll pull up the dashboard, quick note the dashboard numbers are a little lagged by 10-15 minutes.
00:21 Raj: that's fine, just want the general trend. last week we saw 32% overall hit rate on the KV/prefix combined, is that right?
00:30 Omar: yeah about that, the combined is 33.8% over the 14 day window, prefix-only around 18%, KV-only around 15%, but there's overlap so combined is ~34%.
00:44 Maya: and that's across product desc prompts plus the cart summarization prompts?
00:49 Omar: correct, product desc templates are the biggest source of prefix hits because they reuse the leading system prompt and product attributes. cart summarization is less reuse-y, so lower hit.
00:55 Sofia: our goal is to hit at least 60% so we can justify bursting to dedicated nodes, otherwise cost per token is still high.
01:03 Lina: yep makes sense. quick question on methodology: how are keys generated today in the KV cache?
01:10 Omar: currently key is hashed by full prompt blob including template filled values, there is a separate prefix key if the prefix matches exactly, but small differences in whitespace or punctuation do cause misses.
01:24 Raj: so if product attribute ordering changes, we lose the key match?
01:28 Omar: yep, right now ordering and trivial spacing changes matter. we can normalize but there's a tradeoff with false positives if we over-normalize.
01:36 Sofia: what about TTLs? we saw some eviction spikes at midnight on 8/12.
01:41 Omar: TTL is 72 hours default for this env, but our eviction is also LRU based on memory pressure on the node. the midnight spike was due to a batch job that warmed a lot of new entries then memory pressure forced a sweep.
01:55 Raj: can we pin hot keys or reserve more memory?
02:00 Omar: yes, on Dedicated you can reserve a hotkey set and increase memory quota; for hosted we can suggest config changes that bias eviction. also cache warming scripts helped last week when we prefilled top 50 product templates.
02:14 Maya: I noticed a lot of the misses are small changes to the prompt like adding a trailing period or changing SKU order, is there a recommended prompt reuse strategy?
02:23 Omar: a couple of approaches: 1) template normalization on client side — reorder attributes, normalize punctuation; 2) use stronger prefix caching for the fixed system prompt and only hash the variable part for KV; 3) introduce a short window similarity match to map close prompts to the same key, but that's more complex.
02:39 Lina: quick interjection: remind that stronger prefix caching usually yields low latency savings because you avoid re-computation of the shoulder tokens, but it depends on how much you reuse.
02:47 Sofia: yes, product pages are identical for 60% of SKUs, so prefix caching seems promising.
02:52 Raj: what's realistic improvement if we do both normalization and prefix caching?
02:56 Omar: ballpark: normalization could reduce misses by 12-18 pts, prefix caching another 20 pts for product flow, so combined could plausibly reach 60-70% for the product-related workload, overall maybe 55-65% depending on cart/checkout flows.
03:12 Maya: great. any risk to quality if we normalize? we don't want to change the model output semantics.
03:18 Omar: you can normalize order/punctuation without changing semantic tokens that affect output; we should run A/B on a sample to ensure no regressions. that's one of the action items.
03:28 Sofia: can you walk through the recent 'cold start' experiment you ran? the one where you prefetched top 5k products?
03:33 Omar: sure, quick recap: we prefilled 5k most-viewed product prompts into the KV store during off-hours, then ran a synthetic spike against the store. Cold miss rate dropped from 40% to 18% for those SKUs in the first 6 hours. However memory pressure increased and triggered eviction for less-used keys.
03:51 Raj: that explains the midnight sweep. what's the storage footprint?
03:54 Omar: the 5k prefill took ~8GB on the node; our cluster had 64GB but other processes increased memory use. On Dedicated we can bump memory or dedicate nodes to caching.
04:08 Lina: question from execs — what's the perf delta you'd expect moving to dedicated nodes versus hosted for this workload? latency and cost-wise?
04:16 Omar: latency median token delta is probably ~8-12ms improvement per token because of reduced multiplexing and larger KV memory. Cost wise depends on throughput but dedicated is more predictable; we'll run a focused perf test to provide numbers next week.
04:29 Raj: ok we want that perf test. schedule it with Raj and Omar.
04:32 Maya: security question — do we have access logs for cache reads/writes? auditors want to see who touches keys and when.
04:38 Carlos: yes the platform logs cache events with user request ids, timestamp, and node id; we can push those into your SIEM via connector. Note: we do redact prompt content at rest unless you opt-in to retention.
04:51 Sofia: do you store raw prompts for debugging?
04:54 Carlos: default is no. we store hashes and metadata; you can opt-in to store raw inputs but that requires an agreement. Also SOC2 and SSO details are in the security pack we sent last month.
05:07 Raj: ok good. on instrumentation, can we get per-route hourly hit rates? current dashboard is daily.
05:12 Omar: yes we can enable hourly aggregation, it's a config flip on the dashboard side; cost is small. We'll enable it and share the link.
05:19 Sofia: one more thing — are there config knobs for batching that affect cache behavior?
05:24 Omar: batching is orthogonal but it changes request grouping which can increase effective reuse in the runtime; prefix cache is unaffected. If you batch similar requests together you can amortize KV lookups. But large batches can increase tail latency if not tuned.
05:39 Raj: we saw some interpolation in tail latencies last Thursday when batch size spiked.
05:43 Omar: yes that's probably due to request fan-in; we'll add a policy to cap batch size for low-latency routes.
05:50 Lina: let's go through the concrete numbers from last week's runs — Omar you pulled a quick chart?
05:56 Omar: yep, chart up — apologies the transcript may misread but numbers: overall hit-rate 33.8%, token-savings 18% (estimated from cached token avoids), median latency for cached responses 45ms vs non-cached 120ms, 95th 250ms non-cached.
06:14 Sofia: those token-savings numbers are promising but not enough yet. we need to see cost delta for our monthly traffic.
06:20 Lina: we'll prepare a cost projection with current hit rates vs target 60% and share.
06:25 Maya: moving on — prompt reuse strategy, can Redwood provide a client-side library for normalization?
06:31 Omar: yes we have a small JS/Go lib we can share, it's not fully hardened but it's a starting point. We'll put it in the repo link.
06:38 Raj: please include examples for reordering JSON attributes and stripping punctuation.
06:42 Omar: will do.
06:44 Sofia: we also want a test-ground to validate there's no quality regression when we normalize. can Redwood run a blinded A/B on a 2k sample?
06:52 Omar: yes we can run an eval, we just need the sample and the success criteria.
06:56 Sofia: success criteria: no more than 1.5% drop in relevance score across sample and manual spot checks to pass.
07:05 Lina: noted. Omar will run the A/B and provide results.
07:09 Omar: action item for me.
07:12 Raj: one technical question — does the KV cache key include model name and temperature?
07:18 Omar: yes we include model_id and generation params in the key by default, temperature is ignored for deterministic calls in our config but you can opt to include or exclude parameters.
07:29 Maya: helpful. in our case we want deterministic, so exclude temp and seed.
07:33 Omar: noted.
07:35 Sofia: bandwidth — any gating factors for scaling the KV store beyond memory, like network egress or serialization CPU?
07:42 Omar: CPU serialization for large prompt blobs can be heavy, also network IOPS if you shard across nodes. We recommend trimming stored blobs to minimal needed fields (hash + small metadata).
07:54 Raj: can we store a trimmed canonical representation instead of raw prompt?
07:57 Omar: yes that's the recommended approach.
08:00 Lina: quick recap of decisions: 1) try client-side normalization + stronger prefix caching 2) prefill top 5k product templates before promo weekend 3) run A/B eval to check quality 4) schedule dedicated-node perf run. anyone disagree?
08:17 Sofia: agree with caveats on A/B.
08:19 Raj: agree.
08:20 Maya: agree.
08:22 Lina: ok action items as recorded, we'll follow up via slack.
08:26 Carlos: i'll share the dashboard link and security pack again.
08:29 Omar: i'll export hit rate CSV and put recommended TTLs in the doc.
08:33 Lina: raj and omar schedule perf test for week of 25th, maya to confirm stakeholders.
08:38 Sofia: one last question — how quickly can you move TTL from 72h to 7 days in hosted?
08:44 Omar: technically quick but higher memory cost; we can try a 7-day experiment in a restricted env for a week to gauge impact.
08:52 Raj: let's do the experiment.
08:54 Lina: great. any other items?
09:00 Maya: no that's all. thanks.
09:03 Lina: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and next steps.

End of transcript. Notes: some mis-attributions and small transcription errors likely (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of Dedicated).
